note: fpm_iir.c had no mutation set at all until FPM_iir_filt_block was written (finding F8161).  The block form is one statement, so most of this set attacks the ENGINE it inlines -- the asymmetric clamp and the two rounding asymmetries that `FPM_iir_filt`'s own file header says must be preserved -- plus the two things the block form adds: the write-back position and the direction of the walk.

`sections == 0` is not attacked, because it is not tested: the object writes back a register it never assigns on that path, so there is no reference behaviour to compare against (deviation D393).  A mutation there would be recorded against a claim nobody makes.

label: the block filters every sample but the last
find:
for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
		samples[i] = FPM_iir_filt(samples[i], coeff, state, sections);
replace:
for (i = 0; i < count - 1; i++)
		samples[i] = FPM_iir_filt(samples[i], coeff, state, sections);

label: the block is filtered back to front
replace:
samples[count - 1 - i] = FPM_iir_filt(samples[count - 1 - i],
						      coeff, state, sections);

why: A CODEGEN CLAIM, NOT A BEHAVIOURAL ONE, AND THIS TIER CANNOT REACH IT. `(short)ff` is congruent to `ff` modulo 65536, and the whole expression is narrowed to `short` again on assignment, so `(short)((short)ff + x)` and `(short)(ff + x)` agree on EVERY input by construction -- there is no history, coefficient set or clamp state that separates them, and widening the fixture cannot help. What the inner cast buys is the object's own `movswl %cx,%ecx` at 0x0a8bc8: without it GCC 3.4.2 has no reason to emit that instruction. So the claim is real, it is adjudicated by `make similarity` and `byteident.py`, and it is recorded here as equivalent rather than deleted so that nobody re-derives the same negative result. It expires if the harness ever gains an instruction-level observable (tiers.md, F651).
